Patolli is a historic Mesoamerican game,: Patolli is a historic Mesoamerican game, but surviving accounts vary. Ixchel's gold-stake match is a house-rule adaptation, not a claim to reproduce every historical version.
Toss five beans. One to four marked bean: Toss five beans. One to four marked beans move that many spaces; five marked beans move ten. A piece leaves reserve only on a toss of exactly one, landing on its own start square. A toss of zero passes the turn in this house-rule version.
Move clockwise around the 52-space X-sha: Move clockwise around the 52-space X-shaped track. You must land exactly at HOME; a move that overshoots is illegal. No piece may share a space. You may capture one opposing piece only on a marked center crossroads; it returns to reserve and its matched wager is claimed.
The two marked penalty triangles send on: The two marked penalty triangles send one wager unit to the pot. Landing on either marked end square grants another turn. Here, six matched gold wagers are played as one short match: the first to claim four wins; if all six resolve without a majority, it is a draw. This wager-and-scoring system is Ixchel's local variation. Gold is fictional, and no expedition time passes.
